clue.text: Check opening for caretaker

definitions.note: used adjectivally, as in a caretaker government

blocks.note: to check something is to halt it
an opening or space

explanation.surface: Someone inspects the doorway on behalf of the building's janitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caretaker' reads as the janitor, but here it is the adjective meaning temporary, as in a caretaker manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a temporary measure filling in until something permanent arrives, just like a caretaker arrangement.

clue.text: QC in second class

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
ilk means kind or class

explanation.surface: A senior lawyer is enrolled in a second-tier category.
explanation.walkthrough: A QC (Queen's Counsel) is a senior British barrister, who 'takes silk' on appointment and wears a silk gown.
explanation.definitionFit: Silk is the informal British term for a senior barrister, from the silk gown worn.

clue.text: Spinster's game

blocks.note: first meaning: an old-fashioned term for an unmarried woman
second meaning: a card game in which players avoid being left with the odd queen

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes it sound like a pastime belonging to a spinster; the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dated term for an unmarried older woman is also the name of a simple children's card game of pairs.

clue.text: What a soldier may have on in fine film

definitions.text: What a soldier may have on

blocks.note: fine and great both mean excellent
a film is a thin layer, as is a coat of paint

explanation.surface: A soldier could appear in a fine war movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Film looks like a movie, but it is a thin covering layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A greatcoat is a heavy overcoat, classically part of military uniform.

clue.text: Always going up to Montpelier, a criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A fugitive criminal is always heading north to Montpelier.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder runs right through 'up to Montpelier, a'; even the small words count.
explanation.definitionFit: Perpetual motion is the impossible state of a machine that keeps running forever without energy input.

clue.text: Groom leader of Hispanic American group

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front letter, so only the opening of the next word is kept

blocks.note: first letter of the word
US is the standard abbreviation for American
a band is a group, of people or musicians

explanation.surface: A stable hand looks after the horse of a Latino band's frontman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' looks like a verb or a stable hand; it is the man at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A groom is a bridegroom, the man getting married, who thereby becomes a husband.

clue.text: Brand new item from carpenter shouldn't be defective?

definitions.text: Brand new item from carpenter shouldn't be defective?

blocks.clueFragment: Brand new item from carpenter shouldn't be defective?
blocks.note: surface reading: freshly made joinery ought to be free of faults, with every fixing tight
setter's reading: an idiom for being mentally unhinged, pictured literally as a badly fastened piece of woodwork

explanation.surface: A newly made cabinet from the joiner ought not to have faults.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for being a bit crazy is pictured literally as a loose fixing in new carpentry.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be slightly mad, with a mental fault pictured as a mechanical one in a fixing.

clue.text: Work out volume in one

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for single

blocks.note: sole means one and only
V is the abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: Calculate the volume within a single shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Work out reads like exercise; here it is to find a solution.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve a problem is to work out its answer.

clue.text: A married girl in the USA

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for married
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A wedded young woman living in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places the girl in the USA; really 'in' links wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: America is the everyday name for the United States of America.

clue.text: Having good taste, Cinders poured out gin cocktail

indicators.note: something poured out spills and loses its form, so these letters are jumbled
a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cinderella, a woman of refined taste, mixes a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: Cinders is Cinderella's nickname in the pantomime; here it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A discerning person judges well and shows refined taste.

clue.text: Deposit for gatehouse

blocks.note: first meaning: to place or ... something, as with a bank or complaint
second meaning: the small house at the gates of an estate

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it sounds like paying a deposit on a gatehouse; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge a document is to deposit it formally, and a lodge is the porter's house at an estate entrance.

clue.text: Right one developing small firearms

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
something that evolves or develops
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: The correct person is working on miniature guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small firearms' looks like one phrase, but small only supplies a letter; the definition is firearms alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolvers are handguns with a rotating cylinder, a common type of firearm.

clue.text: Simultaneously, however

blocks.note: first meaning: occurring together, in the same moment
second meaning: used to introduce a contrasting point, like nevertheless

explanation.walkthrough: Two adverbs placed side by side; the phrase serves both as 'together in time' and as the concessive 'nonetheless'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means concurrently, and idiomatically introduces a qualification, much as 'but' or 'nevertheless' would.

clue.text: Hearing, sadly, about graduate's lengthy scolding

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so the letters fall out of order
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the degree

blocks.note: the seven letters rearranged
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate; the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A graduate's disciplinary hearing ends, sadly, in a long telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive on graduate's supplies a letter: the degree with an S.
explanation.definitionFit: An earbashing is British slang for a long harangue or telling-off.

clue.text: Sound coming from car with disc on

indicators.note: with means accompanied by, so one piece is placed next to the other

blocks.note: a German make of car
a disc is round like the letter O, which is added on at the end

explanation.surface: Music plays from a car stereo with a CD loaded.
explanation.walkthrough: A disc is O by its round shape; 'on' places it after the car maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio is the sound component of a recording or broadcast, as opposed to the video.

clue.text: In doubt, new curate about new home

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the letters of the clergyman are rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next abbreviation

blocks.note: rearranged letters of the clergyman
N is the abbreviation for new
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A newly appointed curate is unsure about his new parish house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' appears twice: the first shakes up curate, the second is just N, tucked after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncertain means unsure or doubtful, so someone in doubt is uncertain.

clue.text: Land of Hope and Glory's fourth air aunt and I performed

indicators.note: fourth tells us to keep only the letter in that position of the word before it
performed suggests something worked up and reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: fourth letter of the word
letters taken as written, the joining word aside

explanation.surface: The patriotic song is sung by a relative and me.
explanation.walkthrough: Land of Hope and Glory is an Elgar anthem, but Hope is Anthony Hope, author of The Prisoner of Zenda, set in this imaginary kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the fictional central European kingdom invented by the novelist Anthony Hope.

clue.text: Delivery securing wicket before end of league game

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece wraps round another
before places the wrapped unit ahead of the final letter
'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'league'

blocks.note: in cricket each delivery by the bowler is a ball
a wicket is also a small gate or door
final letter of league

explanation.surface: A cricket ball takes a wicket just before the season's finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface points at stumps, but wicket is the old word for a small gate, wrapped inside the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a table game in which balls are struck into pins and holes, a forerunner of pinball.

clue.text: Dumplings and odd-looking conch collected by soldier

indicators.note: odd-looking means strange in appearance, so the letters take an unusual shape
collected by means taken up inside, so the jumbled letters sit within the soldier

blocks.note: GI is an American soldier
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier gathers dumplings and a strange seashell.
explanation.walkthrough: A conch is a large spiral seashell.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are small Italian dumplings, usually made from potato or semolina.

clue.text: Bird, yellow, all but head

indicators.note: keeping everything except the head means dropping the opening letter

blocks.note: yellow means cowardly, which is craven

explanation.surface: A bird is described as yellow except for its head.
explanation.walkthrough: Yellow looks like plumage colour, but it means cowardly here.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black corvid, a well-known bird.

clue.text: Finding of court in support of composer

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting something means sitting underneath it, so one piece comes after the other

blocks.note: Giuseppe Verdi, the Italian opera composer
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A court ruling comes out in favour of a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finding of court' reads as the whole definition, but court is wordplay and only Finding defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is the decision or finding reached by a jury or judge.

clue.text: Eventually seeing rather remarkable rare lot

indicators.note: remarkable suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are put into an unusual order

blocks.note: as in 'I would sooner', meaning I would rather
the seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An auction viewer will eventually spot an unusual and rare lot.
explanation.walkthrough: Rather is the adverb of preference, so it is sooner, not the anagram signal it might seem.
explanation.definitionFit: Sooner or later means at some point in the future, inevitably, which is what eventually expresses.

clue.text: Freighter's crew?

indicators.note: the possessive says the crew belongs to, and so is held within, the vessel's name

blocks.note: letters two to six of the word

explanation.surface: Who mans a cargo ship?
explanation.walkthrough: A rowing crew of eight oarsmen is called an eight; it is sitting inside the cargo ship's name.
explanation.definitionFit: In rowing, an eight is a boat crewed by eight rowers, and so the crew itself.

clue.text: Raise back

blocks.note: first meaning: to bring up, as children or livestock
second meaning: the hind part of something

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like lifting your back; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children is to bring them up, and the rear is the back part of anything.

clue.text: Noticing novel written by Oscar under an assumed name

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the letters are arranged in a new way
written by places the next piece directly beside the rearranged word

blocks.note: the eight letters rearranged
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone spots a book by Oscar Wilde published under a pseudonym.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel and written by suggest a book by Oscar Wilde; novel is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Incognito means with one's identity concealed, typically by adopting a false name.

clue.text: Racket revealed by informer, one inside

indicators.note: inside places the numeral within the word for the informer

blocks.note: a nose is slang for a police informer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A criminal scam is exposed by a grass on the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Racket looks like a criminal scheme, as an informer would expose; it means din.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud, unpleasant din, which is simply noise.

clue.text: Reflect it's good to pay attention

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
to listen is to pay attention to what is said

explanation.surface: Advice that thinking things over means it is good to pay attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Reflect looks like 'think carefully', but it is the light sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to shine with reflected light, as wet surfaces do, so to reflect brightly.

clue.text: Former player, demanding type

blocks.note: ex means former
an actor plays parts on stage

explanation.surface: A retired performer is known for being difficult and demanding.
explanation.walkthrough: Player suggests sport, but it is a stage player.
explanation.definitionFit: An exactor is one who exacts, insisting on payment or obedience, so a demanding person.
